title: Periodicity of a sequence
summary: Exact repetition after a fixed positive index shift.

context.framework: sequences indexed by integers or natural numbers
context.note: Context is named textually in this seed release; its foundations are not yet recursively expanded into QEVA records.

assumptions.text: A sequence (a_n) has an index domain on which n+p is defined for the stated n.

content.plain: A periodic sequence repeats exactly after some fixed positive number of steps.
content.exact: A sequence (a_n) is periodic with period p>0 iff a_{n+p}=a_n for every index n for which both terms are in the domain. A least positive such p, when it exists, is called the fundamental period.
content.caveat: Continuous functions, group actions, tilings, and dynamical systems use related but context-specific notions of periodicity.

relations.note: Quasiperiodicity can exhibit recurrent structure without one global exact finite period.

verification.method: QEVA seed formulation checked editorially for mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.
